sentences.en: President Erdogan comes to power in 2002.
sentences.zh: 埃尔多安总统于2002年上台。

sentences.en: And he begins to consolidate power very quickly.
sentences.zh: 他开始非常迅速地巩固权力。

sentences.en: Recep Tayyip Erdogan, his country's most powerful leader since Atatürk himself.
sentences.zh: 雷杰普·塔伊普·埃尔多安，他是自凯末尔本人以来该国最有权势的领导人。
zh_words: 雷杰普·塔伊普·埃尔多安

sentences.en: And President Erdogan starts, for lack of a better word, bullying everything in the country.
sentences.zh: 埃尔多安总统开始——用一个词来形容——霸凌国内的一切。

sentences.en: The country continues to slide towards authoritarianism as Mr. Erdogan continues to consolidate power.
sentences.zh: 随着埃尔多安先生不断巩固权力，这个国家继续滑向威权主义。

sentences.en: He bullies dissent.
sentences.zh: 他霸凌异见者。

sentences.en: What we've seen over the last years is Erdogan consolidating power, trampling human rights, freedom of the press, freedom of assembly.
sentences.zh: 过去几年我们看到的是，埃尔多安在巩固权力，践踏人权、新闻自由和集会自由。

sentences.en: He bullies journalists.
sentences.zh: 他霸凌记者。

sentences.en: We know that he's jailed about 76 journalists.
sentences.zh: 我们知道他已经监禁了大约76名记者。

sentences.en: When it comes to things like human rights, he's extremely backward.
sentences.zh: 在人权等方面，他极其落后。

sentences.en: And he bullies the economy.
sentences.zh: 他还霸凌经济。

sentences.en: For Turkey, the year proved to be a prosperous one, with GDP growth at more than 7%, an impressive sum when you consider
sentences.zh: 对于土耳其来说，这一年被证明是繁荣的一年，GDP增长超过7%，考虑到

sentences.en: the turmoil in Europe and the Middle EaSt. What does it mean to bully the economy?
sentences.zh: 欧洲和中东的动荡，这是一个令人印象深刻的数字。霸凌经济是什么意思？

sentences.en: What does that actually look like?
sentences.zh: 那实际上是什么样子的？

sentences.en: The ruling Justice and Development Party came to power in 2002.
sentences.zh: 执政的正义与发展党于2002年上台。

sentences.en: Since then, Turkey has enjoyed strong growth, development, and renewed prosperity for many.
sentences.zh: 从那时起，土耳其享受了强劲的增长、发展，并为许多人带来了新的繁荣。

sentences.en: It really means growth.
sentences.zh: 这实际上意味着增长。

sentences.en: Major infrastructure projects became the AK Party's hallmark.
sentences.zh: 大型基础设施项目成为了正发党的标志。

sentences.en: Building more roads, fast trains, and airports, including this one built on a man-made island.
sentences.zh: 修建更多的道路、高铁和机场，包括这个建在人工岛上的机场。

sentences.en: That the president was so focused on growth that he did all of these building projects to try to get there.
sentences.zh: 总统如此专注于增长，以至于他为了实现这一目标，进行了所有这些建设项目。

sentences.en: He builds schools, he builds mosques, he builds roads, builds things in basically every city in Turkey, all of which gooses the economy.
sentences.zh: 他建学校、建清真寺、建道路，在土耳其几乎每个城市都搞建设，所有这些都刺激了经济。

sentences.en: Big construction projects multiplied and the economy grew.
sentences.zh: 大型建筑项目成倍增加，经济也随之增长。

sentences.en: Annual income per person has tripled since 2002 to almost $11,000.
sentences.zh: 自2002年以来，人均年收入增长了两倍，达到近11000美元。

sentences.en: Erdogan is a classic populist, someone who makes big promises to people and then hands out favors, whether it's a construction project in your backyard or a
sentences.zh: 埃尔多安是一位典型的民粹主义者，他向人们做出宏大的承诺，然后分发恩惠，无论是你家后院的建设项目还是

sentences.en: government contract, to keep his supporters happy.
sentences.zh: 政府合同，以此来让他的支持者满意。

sentences.en: His populist way of running the economy is lots of projects and favors, lots of growth, and lots of reward for the people who support him.
sentences.zh: 他管理经济的民粹主义方式就是大量的项目和恩惠，大量的增长，以及对他支持者的大量回报。

sentences.en: And Jim, how did Erdogan pay for all of this rapid growth, these projects that start going up all over the country?
sentences.zh: 那么吉姆，埃尔多安是如何为所有这些快速增长以及全国各地兴起的项目买单的呢？

sentences.en: Well, you can only pay for government spending in a relatively limited number of ways.
sentences.zh: 嗯，政府支出的资金来源相对有限。

sentences.en: You can happen to have a bunch of natural riches like a sovereign oil fund, which Turkey does not, or you can raise taxes or borrow money.
sentences.zh: 你要么拥有像主权石油基金那样的自然财富（土耳其没有），要么就是增加税收或借钱。

sentences.en: And in this case, he prints money, borrows money, and Turkey finances its projects that way.
sentences.zh: 在这种情况下，他印钞、借钱，土耳其就是这样为项目融资的。

sentences.en: Merhaba.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Welcome to Turkey, a cradle of civilizations and cultures throughout history.
sentences.zh: 欢迎来到土耳其，这里是历史上文明与文化的摇篮。

sentences.en: Turkey is now welcoming investors from all over the world.
sentences.zh: 土耳其现在欢迎来自世界各地的投资者。

sentences.en: And a lot of it is borrowed from foreigners.
sentences.zh: 其中很大一部分是从外国人那里借来的。

sentences.en: So basically, he is doing this all through debt.
sentences.zh: 所以基本上，他所做的一切都是通过债务完成的。

sentences.en: Yeah.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Investors can access the agency's website at www.inveSt.gov.tr.
sentences.zh: 投资者可以访问该机构的网站www.invest.gov.tr。

sentences.en: So when all these projects got off the ground, all this building by this populist leader, were the people of Turkey generally happy?
sentences.zh: 那么，当所有这些项目启动，这位民粹主义领导人进行所有这些建设时，土耳其人民普遍感到高兴吗？

sentences.en: Did it work?
sentences.zh: 这奏效了吗？

sentences.en: Yeah, they keep re-electing him.
sentences.zh: 是的，他们不断地重新选举他。

sentences.en: And granted, there are questions about those elections.
sentences.zh: 当然，人们对这些选举存在质疑。

sentences.en: But yeah, they keep re-electing him.
sentences.zh: 但确实，他们不断地重新选举他。

sentences.en: And there is a lot of economic growth, growth levels that helped consolidate his popularity among the people of Turkey.
sentences.zh: 而且确实有大量的经济增长，这种增长水平有助于巩固他在土耳其人民中的受欢迎程度。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Join this exciting journey.
sentences.zh: 加入这段激动人心的旅程。

sentences.en: Now is the time.
sentences.zh: 现在正是时候。

sentences.en: Come and secure the future of your investments.
sentences.zh: 快来确保你的投资未来。

sentences.en: Invest in Turkey.
sentences.zh: 投资土耳其。

sentences.en: So when did things start to change in Turkey?
sentences.zh: 那么土耳其的情况是从什么时候开始改变的呢？

sentences.en: So this week, the Turkish people woke up and found, almost overnight, that their currency, the lira, was worth dramatically less than it had been.
sentences.zh: 本周，土耳其人民醒来后发现，几乎在一夜之间，他们的货币里拉的价值比以前大幅缩水。

sentences.en: At the end of March, the exchange rate of lira to the dollar was about four lira to one dollar.
sentences.zh: 3月底，里拉兑美元的汇率约为4里拉兑1美元。

sentences.en: By the end of the day, on Tuesday, it was almost seven lira to a dollar.
sentences.zh: 到周二收盘时，几乎变成了7里拉兑1美元。

sentences.en: It's the worst collapse of their currency since 2001.
sentences.zh: 这是自2001年以来他们货币最严重的崩溃。

sentences.en: So how did this actually happen?
sentences.zh: 那么这到底是怎么发生的呢？

sentences.en: And how does it relate to how Erdogan has managed the economy?
sentences.zh: 这与埃尔多安管理经济的方式有什么关系？

sentences.en: So Erdogan is a type of leader who has many more levers at his disposal for running an economy than the president of the United States does.
sentences.zh: 埃尔多安这类领导人在管理经济时，比美国总统拥有更多的手段。

sentences.en: He basically controls fiscal policy, what gets spent and how it gets spent.
sentences.zh: 他基本上控制着财政政策，即支出什么以及如何支出。

sentences.en: He also controls, essentially through his influence on the central bank, monetary policy,
sentences.zh: 他还通过对中央银行的影响力，实质上控制着货币政策，

sentences.en: which is not something that the president of the United States would actually have influence over.
sentences.zh: 而这并不是美国总统实际上能够施加影响的事情。

sentences.en: And so that allows him to basically pull all of the levers at the same time in favor of economic growth with very little regard for what economists would consider to be
sentences.zh: 这使他能够基本上同时拉动所有杠杆来促进经济增长，而几乎不考虑经济学家所认为的

sentences.en: the big risks of inflation.
sentences.zh: 通货膨胀的巨大风险。

sentences.en: And what were those risks?
sentences.zh: 那些风险是什么？

sentences.en: Interest rates, as you know, are the rate at which you borrow money and have to pay it back with intereSt.
sentences.zh: 利率，如你所知，是你借钱并必须连本带利偿还的比率。

sentences.en: If you spend too much money, particularly borrowed money, while keeping interest rates very low
sentences.zh: 如果你在保持极低利率的同时花费过多的钱，特别是借来的钱，

sentences.en: and you rev economic growth up very, very high, faster than the level which economists generally think your economy is capable of performing.
sentences.zh: 并且你将经济增长推得非常、非常高，超过了经济学家普遍认为你的经济所能承受的水平。

sentences.en: If you do all that for too long of a time, prices and wages start to rise very quickly.
sentences.zh: 如果你在太长的时间里这样做，价格和工资就会开始迅速上涨。

sentences.en: It's what economists call overheating.
sentences.zh: 这就是经济学家所说的过热。

sentences.en: And when you start to see overheating, you can get massive spirals of inflation and then you're in real trouble.
sentences.zh: 当你开始看到过热时，你可能会陷入大规模的通胀螺旋，然后你就真的陷入麻烦了。

sentences.en: So it sounds like Erdogan is disregarding the basic economic principles that govern most of the global financial system.
sentences.zh: 听起来埃尔多安无视了统治全球金融体系大部分的基本经济原则。

sentences.en: I would go even farther than that.
sentences.zh: 我会说得更远一点。

sentences.en: He's not just disregarding those principles.
sentences.zh: 他不仅仅是无视这些原则。

sentences.en: He is actively defying them.
sentences.zh: 他是在积极地对抗它们。

sentences.en: He doesn't believe that raising interest rates will slow inflation as basically every other central bank in the world believes.
sentences.zh: 他不相信提高利率会减缓通胀，而世界上几乎所有其他中央银行都相信这一点。

sentences.en: He believes high interest rates cause inflation.
sentences.zh: 他认为高利率会导致通胀。

sentences.en: This is something he's long held.
sentences.zh: 这是他长期持有的观点。

sentences.en: He believes high interest rates are evil.
sentences.zh: 他认为高利率是邪恶的。

sentences.en: Almost no economists agree with that.
sentences.zh: 几乎没有经济学家同意这一点。

sentences.en: Very little historical evidence would support that.
sentences.zh: 几乎没有什么历史证据能支持这一点。

sentences.en: And so when it comes time for him to try to control inflation, when he's faced with this inflation crisis that's brewing in his country, he can't just imprison it.
sentences.zh: 所以当他需要尝试控制通胀时，当他面对国内正在酝酿的这场通胀危机时，他不能仅仅把通胀关进监狱。

sentences.en: You can't just lock away price increases.
sentences.zh: 你不能仅仅把物价上涨锁起来。

sentences.en: You can try all these different things, price caps, whatever.
sentences.zh: 你可以尝试所有这些不同的方法，价格上限，等等。

sentences.en: They don't work.
sentences.zh: 它们都不起作用。

sentences.en: Typically, what economists say is you need to raise interest rates.
sentences.zh: 通常，经济学家会说你需要提高利率。

sentences.en: And he so far has been unwilling to do that, again, because he believes that raising interest rates will just cause more inflation.
sentences.zh: 而他到目前为止一直不愿这样做，同样是因为他认为提高利率只会导致更多的通胀。

sentences.en: So, Jim, we have an increasingly authoritarian leader who thinks he can bully the politics in his country and even the economics.
sentences.zh: 所以，吉姆，我们有一位日益威权化的领导人，他认为自己可以霸凌国内的政治，甚至经济。

sentences.en: He's borrowing lots of money to fulfill his populist mission.
sentences.zh: 他为了实现他的民粹主义使命而借了大量的钱。

sentences.en: Where does this all lead?
sentences.zh: 这一切会导致什么结果？

sentences.en: Well, if you borrow money based on artificially low interest rates for too long and keep growth going for too long, there could be a moment,
sentences.zh: 嗯，如果你基于人为的低利率借钱太久，并让增长持续太久，可能会有一个时刻，

sentences.en: and this seems to have happened to Turkey, where investors wake up and say, we're just not sure about this anymore.
sentences.zh: 这似乎已经在土耳其发生了，投资者醒悟过来并说，我们对此不再确定了。

sentences.en: And they just overnight flip on you.
sentences.zh: 然后他们一夜之间就背弃了你。

sentences.en: And that really appears to be what has happened.
sentences.zh: 这看起来确实就是所发生的事情。

sentences.en: And by flipping on Turkey, what does that actually mean?
sentences.zh: 那么，背弃土耳其，这实际上意味着什么？

sentences.en: What are they doing?
sentences.zh: 他们在做什么？

sentences.en: They're selling lira.
sentences.zh: 他们在抛售里拉。

sentences.en: They are getting their money out of the country.
sentences.zh: 他们正在把钱撤出这个国家。

sentences.en: And that is a flight of financing and of investment that just absolutely can devastate an economy.
sentences.zh: 这是一种融资和投资的逃离，绝对可以摧毁一个经济体。

sentences.en: And lower the value of currency.
sentences.zh: 并降低货币的价值。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Absolutely.
sentences.zh: 绝对是这样。

sentences.en: What happens is if a bunch of international bankers own a bunch of assets in lira or just own a bunch of lira and they sell them all at once,
sentences.zh: 发生的情况是，如果一群国际银行家拥有大量里拉资产，或者只是拥有大量里拉，然后他们一次性全部卖出，

sentences.en: that dramatically reduces the price of lira.
sentences.zh: 这会大幅降低里拉的价格。

sentences.en: But more importantly, it sends a signal to future investors like, hey, this is something to be worried about.
sentences.zh: 但更重要的是，它向未来的投资者发出了一个信号，比如，嘿，这是一个值得担心的问题。

sentences.en: This is a thing to be panicked about.
sentences.zh: 这是一个值得恐慌的事情。

sentences.en: And you get to a place where, like we saw in recent days.
sentences.zh: 然后你就会到达一个像我们最近几天看到的那样的境地。

sentences.en: The president, Erdogan, has to stand up on TV and essentially beg his people.
sentences.zh: 埃尔多安总统不得不站在电视上，本质上是在乞求他的人民。

sentences.en: If there is anyone who has dollars, euros or gold under their pillows, they should go exchange it for Turkish liras at our banks.
sentences.zh: 如果有人枕头下有美元、欧元或黄金，他们应该去我们的银行兑换成土耳其里拉。

sentences.en: To exchange their dollars or gold or whatever for lira to try to prop up the value of the nation's currency.
sentences.zh: 去把他们的美元或黄金或其他东西兑换成里拉，试图支撑国家货币的价值。

sentences.en: And to counteract the sale of lira by foreign investors.
sentences.zh: 并抵消外国投资者抛售里拉的影响。

sentences.en: Yes.
sentences.zh: 是的。

sentences.en: Okay.
sentences.zh: 好的。

sentences.en: Now, that sounds like a very bad Turkish problem.
sentences.zh: 现在，这听起来像是一个非常糟糕的土耳其问题。

sentences.en: What does it start to mean, if anything, for the rest of the global economy?
sentences.zh: 如果这对全球经济有任何影响的话，它开始意味着什么？

sentences.en: Well, there's a bunch of ways that it can hurt the global economy.
sentences.zh: 嗯，它可以通过多种方式伤害全球经济。

sentences.en: For one, it definitely messes with global trade markets in a weird way.
sentences.zh: 首先，它肯定会以一种奇怪的方式扰乱全球贸易市场。

sentences.en: So, Turkish buyers now can't buy nearly as much from exporters in the developed world, for example.
sentences.zh: 例如，土耳其买家现在无法从发达国家的出口商那里购买那么多东西了。

sentences.en: Because their money isn't worth as much.
sentences.zh: 因为他们的钱不值钱了。

sentences.en: Right.
sentences.zh: 没错。

sentences.en: Like, so the United States, for example, sells about $500 million worth of cotton every year to Turkey.
sentences.zh: 比如，美国每年向土耳其出口价值约5亿美元的棉花。

sentences.en: But now, Turkey is going to be able to buy a lot less than that at this exchange rate.
sentences.zh: 但现在，由于汇率原因，土耳其能买到的量将大幅减少。

sentences.en: They just don't have the buying power that they used to.
sentences.zh: 他们的购买力已大不如前。

sentences.en: At the same time, the United States actually should be able to import a lot more of Turkish goods for cheaper.
sentences.zh: 与此同时，美国实际上应该能以更低的价格进口更多的土耳其商品。

sentences.en: We import like $300 million worth of Turkish rugs every year.
sentences.zh: 我们每年进口价值约3亿美元的土耳其地毯。

sentences.en: And the prices on that, relatively, are going to come down.
sentences.zh: 相对而言，这些商品的价格将会下降。

sentences.en: Because the buying power of the dollar is much higher in regards to Turkish rugs.
sentences.zh: 因为美元在购买土耳其地毯时的购买力大大增强了。

sentences.en: In other words, Turkey is on sale.
sentences.zh: 换句话说，土耳其正在“打折”。

sentences.en: Turkey is on sale.
sentences.zh: 土耳其正在“打折”。

sentences.en: Well, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 嗯，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And then it gets weird when you think about sometimes the United States and Turkey compete with each other in trade as sellers.
sentences.zh: 当你想到美国和土耳其有时作为贸易卖方存在竞争关系时，情况就变得有些微妙了。

sentences.en: So, I'm from Oregon.
sentences.zh: 我来自俄勒冈州。

sentences.en: We sell a lot of hazelnuts from Oregon.
sentences.zh: 我们俄勒冈州销售大量的榛子。

sentences.en: We grow a lot of hazelnuts.
sentences.zh: 我们种植很多榛子。

sentences.en: We sell them on a global market.
sentences.zh: 我们将它们销往全球市场。

sentences.en: China ends up buying, at the end of the day, a lot of those hazelnuts.
sentences.zh: 最终，中国买走了其中很大一部分。

sentences.en: Well, they also buy a lot of Turkish hazelnuts.
sentences.zh: 嗯，他们也购买大量的土耳其榛子。

sentences.en: And now, the Turkish hazelnuts are on sale, and the Oregon hazelnuts, by the way, because of the United States and China's trade dispute at the moment, are on, I don't know,
sentences.zh: 现在，土耳其榛子在“打折”，而顺便提一下，由于目前美中之间的贸易争端，俄勒冈榛子正处于……我不知道该怎么说，

sentences.en: price markup, whatever you call the opposite of being on sale.
sentences.zh: 价格上涨，或者说任何与“打折”相反的说法。

sentences.en: And so, the effect for Oregon farmers could be very bad.
sentences.zh: 因此，这对俄勒冈州的农民来说可能非常糟糕。

sentences.en: That's fascinating.
sentences.zh: 这太引人深思了。

sentences.en: So, this is the way in which one country's decision to not do something about inflation spreads around the globe and begins to hurt other economies.
sentences.zh: 这就是一个国家决定不对通货膨胀采取行动，从而波及全球并开始损害其他经济体的方式。

sentences.en: The other way is that banks in other countries have loans out to businesses in Turkey, or they are bondholders for the Turkish government, or whatever.
sentences.zh: 另一种方式是，其他国家的银行向土耳其企业发放了贷款，或者它们是土耳其政府的债券持有人，诸如此类。

sentences.en: And there is then fear of, well, if the Turkish government decides to massively inflate away its debts, or if they default on debts, or whatever,
sentences.zh: 然后人们就会担心，如果土耳其政府决定通过大规模通胀来抵消债务，或者如果他们债务违约，等等，

sentences.en: then those fears can ripple through to the balance sheets of those banks, which can affect those countries.
sentences.zh: 那么这些担忧就会波及到这些银行的资产负债表，从而影响到这些国家。

sentences.en: Like, if you're worried about a Spanish banking bailout possibility because of exposure to Turkey, this is another way that financial crises spread.
sentences.zh: 比如，如果你担心西班牙银行业可能因对土耳其的风险敞口而需要救助，这就是金融危机蔓延的另一种方式。

sentences.en: And all this is the result of Erdogan essentially going on a building spree, a borrowing spree, and a spree of not raising the interest rate, as you suggested he should.
sentences.zh: 而这一切都是埃尔多安大搞建设、大举借债，以及正如你所建议的那样，拒绝提高利率的结果。

sentences.en: Right, absolutely.
sentences.zh: 没错，绝对是这样。

sentences.en: And it's not just me.
sentences.zh: 而且不仅仅是我这么认为。

sentences.en: It's basically every economist in the world.
sentences.zh: 基本上全世界的经济学家都这么认为。

sentences.en: And there are all these columns coming out just saying, Turkey has a very easy solution to this problem.
sentences.zh: 现在到处都是评论文章，都在说土耳其解决这个问题有一个非常简单的办法。

sentences.en: It just needs to raise interest rates and deal with a little economic pain for a while.
sentences.zh: 只需要提高利率，忍受一段时间的经济阵痛即可。

sentences.en: This is what America did in the 1980s when inflation got very bad.
sentences.zh: 这就是美国在20世纪80年代通胀严重时所采取的做法。

sentences.en: Paul Volcker, then the head of the Fed, raised interest rates.
sentences.zh: 时任美联储主席的保罗·沃尔克提高了利率。

sentences.en: And voila, it produced a mild recession for a little bit.
sentences.zh: 瞧，这在短期内引发了一场温和的衰退。

sentences.en: And then the American economy recovered, and we have not really had an inflation problem since.
sentences.zh: 然后美国经济复苏了，从那以后我们基本上就没再遇到过通胀问题。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Prices go up about 2% a year.
sentences.zh: 物价每年上涨约2%。

sentences.en: You pay $1 for a can of soup this year, and it's $1.02 next year.
sentences.zh: 你今年花1美元买一罐汤，明年就是1.02美元。

sentences.en: Well, in Turkey, inflation is about 16% right now.
sentences.zh: 而在土耳其，目前的通胀率约为16%。

sentences.en: So that's a much, much faster rate at which prices are going up.
sentences.zh: 所以物价上涨的速度要快得多得多。

sentences.en: And if you are a consumer in the Turkish economy, you experience that as, wow, every day that I wake up, the money in my wallet buys a little bit less than it bought yesterday.
sentences.zh: 如果你是土耳其经济中的消费者，你的感受就是：哇，每天醒来，我钱包里的钱买到的东西都比昨天少了一点。

sentences.en: Hmm.
sentences.zh: 嗯。

sentences.en: Why would Erdogan be so resistant to something that seems so simple and foolproof as raising the price of borrowing, raising the interest rate inside Turkey?
sentences.zh: 为什么埃尔多安会如此抗拒提高借贷成本、提高土耳其国内利率这样看起来既简单又万无一失的做法呢？

sentences.en: Well, two reasons.
sentences.zh: 嗯，有两个原因。

sentences.en: One, populist policies are called populist for a reason, because they are meant to be popular.
sentences.zh: 第一，民粹主义政策之所以被称为民粹主义，是有原因的，因为它们旨在迎合大众。

sentences.en: Raising interest rates does not usually very popular.
sentences.zh: 提高利率通常并不受欢迎。

sentences.en: Because it makes borrowing more expensive.
sentences.zh: 因为它增加了借贷成本。

sentences.en: Think about it.
sentences.zh: 试想一下。

sentences.en: If suddenly everyone who went out to buy a home or a car or a new piece of business equipment in the United States had to pay triple the interest rate that they had to pay yesterday,
sentences.zh: 如果美国所有打算买房、买车或购买新商业设备的人，突然都要支付比昨天高出三倍的利率，

sentences.en: and we were all being told that was to ease inflation, you'd have a lot of people who've been saving up their money for a long time on a down payment really angry about, hey,
sentences.zh: 而且我们都被告知这是为了缓解通胀，那么那些长期存钱支付首付的人肯定会非常愤怒，心想：嘿，

sentences.en: I can't borrow money.
sentences.zh: 我借不到钱了。

sentences.en: Also, it tends to push your economy into recession if you have to raise interest rates very abruptly.
sentences.zh: 此外，如果你必须非常突然地提高利率，它往往会把你的经济推向衰退。

sentences.en: It contracts economic activity.
sentences.zh: 它会收缩经济活动。

sentences.en: Many economists see that as the price you pay to stop inflation and to get your economy back on the right footing.
sentences.zh: 许多经济学家认为这是为了遏制通胀、让经济重回正轨所必须付出的代价。

sentences.en: But again, compounding all this is the fact that Erdogan does not agree with most economists.
sentences.zh: 但同样，让这一切雪上加霜的是，埃尔多安并不认同大多数经济学家的观点。

sentences.en: And he, by all accounts, appears to have surrounded himself with advisors who think the way that he does, or at least tell him that they think the way that he does.
sentences.zh: 据各方说法，他似乎身边围绕的都是那些想法与他一致的顾问，或者至少是告诉他他们想法与他一致的顾问。

sentences.en: So in a sense, all this we're talking about is the kind of logical economic consequence of an authoritarian regime, right?
sentences.zh: 所以从某种意义上说，我们谈论的这一切都是威权政权带来的逻辑上的经济后果，对吧？

sentences.en: It seems like we spend so much time talking about, quite naturally and rightly, the consequences of authoritarianism when it comes to people's rights and to democracy.
sentences.zh: 我们似乎花了很多时间在谈论威权主义在人权和民主方面的后果，这很自然，也很正确。

sentences.en: But here we're talking about the economic cost of authoritarianism.
sentences.zh: 但在这里，我们谈论的是威权主义的经济代价。

sentences.en: And is that essentially what we're looking at?
sentences.zh: 这基本上就是我们所看到的吗？

sentences.en: I think so.
sentences.zh: 我想是的。

sentences.en: I think what we are seeing here is, in particular,
sentences.zh: 我认为我们在这里看到的是，特别是，

sentences.en: the cost of an authoritarian government that wants to consolidate all of the levers of economic power into the hands of essentially one man who is not cognizant of when to poll and when not to poll them.
sentences.zh: 一个威权政府的代价，它想要将所有的经济权力杠杆集中在一个人手中，而这个人却不知道何时该拉动、何时不该拉动这些杠杆。

sentences.en: Political goals are always, to some degree, wrapped up with the economy.
sentences.zh: 政治目标在某种程度上总是与经济交织在一起。

sentences.en: But when you run the economy to benefit a ruling party, first and foremost, in the short term, you set yourself up for dramatic longer term or even medium term consequences.
sentences.zh: 但当你为了执政党的利益而运行经济时，首先且最重要的是，你是在为长期的、甚至是中期的严重后果埋下伏笔。

sentences.en: And the thing is, the medium term does arrive.
sentences.zh: 问题在于，中期终究会到来。

sentences.en: The long run eventually becomes the short run.
sentences.zh: 长期最终会变成短期。

sentences.en: And there is a day when you have to pay the consequences of doing a bunch of things just to make yourself look good in the moment.
sentences.zh: 总有一天，你必须为你为了眼前的光鲜而做的一系列事情付出代价。

sentences.en: Jim, thank you very much.
sentences.zh: 吉姆，非常感谢你。

sentences.en: It is my pleasure.
sentences.zh: 这是我的荣幸。

sentences.en: Thank you for having me.
sentences.zh: 谢谢你邀请我。

sentences.en: In a speech on Tuesday, President Erdogan encouraged Turkish citizens to restore the value of the lira by buying domestically made products rather than foreign imports.
sentences.zh: 在周二的一次演讲中，埃尔多安总统鼓励土耳其公民通过购买国产产品而非外国进口商品来恢复里拉的价值。

sentences.en: During the speech, he proposed boycotting U.S.
sentences.zh: 在演讲中，他提议抵制美国

sentences.en: technology, including the iPhone.
sentences.zh: 科技产品，包括iPhone。

sentences.en: We will stand against the dollar, currency rates, inflation, interest rates, he said.
sentences.zh: 他说：“我们将抵御美元、汇率、通胀和利率。”

sentences.en: I believe in my nation.
sentences.zh: 我相信我的国家。

sentences.en: We'll be right back.
sentences.zh: 我们马上回来。

sentences.en: The New York Times app?
sentences.zh: 《纽约时报》应用程序？

sentences.en: Unlocked?
sentences.zh: 解锁了？

sentences.en: Everyone knows you need to subscribe to the Times to access all of the reporting.
sentences.zh: 大家都知道你需要订阅《时报》才能阅读所有报道。

sentences.en: But what if you could explore the Times for a month, for free, without putting in a credit card?
sentences.zh: 但如果能免费试用《时报》一个月，且无需绑定信用卡呢？

sentences.en: Now you can.
sentences.zh: 现在你可以了。

sentences.en: When you download the New York Times app for the first time, your first month in the app is free.
sentences.zh: 当你首次下载《纽约时报》应用程序时，你在应用里的第一个月是免费的。

sentences.en: A month to go behind the paywall to see what Times subscribers get every single day.
sentences.zh: 用一个月的时间突破付费墙，看看《时报》订阅者每天都能获得什么。

sentences.en: If you don't already subscribe to the New York Times, download the Times app today and get free access for 30 days.
sentences.zh: 如果你还没有订阅《纽约时报》，今天就下载《时报》应用程序，获取30天的免费访问权限。

sentences.en: Here's what else you need to know today.
sentences.zh: 以下是你今天还需要了解的其他新闻。

sentences.en: Moments ago, an 884-page report issued unanimously by the 40th statewide investigative grand jury.
sentences.zh: 就在刚才，第40届州级调查大陪审团一致发布了一份884页的报告。

sentences.en: The largest, most comprehensive report into child sexual abuse within the Catholic Church ever produced in the United States was released.
sentences.zh: 这是美国有史以来针对天主教会内部儿童性虐待事件规模最大、最全面的报告。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, a grand jury released a sweeping report about sexual abuse by the Catholic Church in Pennsylvania,
sentences.zh: 周二，一个大陪审团发布了一份关于宾夕法尼亚州天主教会性虐待事件的详尽报告，

sentences.en: identifying more than 300 accused members of the clergy, 1,000 victims, and a systematic 70-year campaign to cover it up.
sentences.zh: 确认了超过300名被指控的神职人员、1000名受害者，以及一场长达70年的系统性掩盖运动。

sentences.en: Dozens of witnesses testified before the grand jury detailing acts of sexual abuse by priests and how senior church officials covered up their criminal conduct,
sentences.zh: 数十名证人在大陪审团面前作证，详细描述了神职人员的性虐待行为，以及教会高层如何掩盖他们的犯罪行为，

sentences.en: prioritizing their institution over the safety and welfare of these young boys and girls.
sentences.zh: 将他们的机构利益置于这些年轻男孩和女孩的安全与福祉之上。

sentences.en: According to the report, church leaders persuaded victims to remain silent about the abuse and police officers not to investigate it.
sentences.zh: 根据报告，教会领袖说服受害者对虐待保持沉默，并劝阻警察不要进行调查。

sentences.en: The revelations are unlikely to lead to criminal charges, given the statute of limitations in Pennsylvania.
sentences.zh: 鉴于宾夕法尼亚州的诉讼时效，这些披露不太可能导致刑事指控。

sentences.en: But abuse survivors and advocates are pushing state lawmakers to change those laws, a move the Catholic Church has opposed.
sentences.zh: 但虐待幸存者和倡导者正在推动州议员修改这些法律，而天主教会对此表示反对。

sentences.en: As the members of the grand jury wrote in their report,
sentences.zh: 正如大陪审团成员在报告中所写的那样，

sentences.en: we need you to hear this.
sentences.zh: 我们需要你们听到这些。

sentences.en: There have been other reports about child sex abuse within the Catholic Church, but never on this scale.
sentences.zh: 之前也有过关于天主教会内部儿童性虐待的报告，但从未达到这种规模。

sentences.en: For many of us, those earlier stories happened someplace else.
sentences.zh: 对我们许多人来说，那些早期的故事发生在别的地方。

sentences.en: Now we know the truth.
sentences.zh: 现在我们知道了真相。

sentences.en: It happened everywhere.
sentences.zh: 它发生在每一个地方。

sentences.en: Buenas.
sentences.zh: 你好。

sentences.en: Perdona la molestia.
sentences.zh: 抱歉打扰了。

sentences.en: On Tuesday, Puerto Rico restored electricity to some of the last residential customers on the island
sentences.zh: 周二，波多黎各恢复了岛上最后一些住宅用户的电力供应，

sentences.en: after a rebuilding process that took nearly a year and cost more than $3 billion.
sentences.zh: 此前重建过程耗时近一年，耗资超过30亿美元。

sentences.en: My colleague, Frances Robles, spoke with one of the final residents to regain power,
sentences.zh: 我的同事弗朗西斯·罗伯斯采访了最后恢复供电的居民之一，

sentences.en: Jasmin Mendez, a 44-year-old mother of three, who has spent 11 months without light or a working refrigerator.
sentences.zh: 44岁的三个孩子的母亲贾斯敏·门德斯，她已经在没有电和冰箱的情况下生活了11个月。

sentences.en: The Times reports that up to 25% of the work done to restore electricity in Puerto Rico may have to be redone.
sentences.zh: 《时报》报道称，波多黎各为恢复电力所做的工作中，高达25%可能需要重做。

sentences.en: And that despite massive investments, the electric system there is in no better shape today than it was before Hurricane Maria.
sentences.zh: 尽管投入了巨额资金，那里的电力系统今天的情况并不比玛丽亚飓风之前好。

sentences.en: That's it for The Daily.
sentences.zh: 以上就是《每日新闻》的全部内容。

sentences.en: I'm Michael Barbaro.
sentences.zh: 我是迈克尔·巴巴罗。

sentences.en: See you tomorrow.
sentences.zh: 明天见。

sentences.en: For decades, the Brooklyn Democratic Party operated as a tightly controlled machine.
sentences.zh: 几十年来，布鲁克林民主党一直像一台受到严密控制的机器一样运作。

sentences.en: Until this summer.
sentences.zh: 直到今年夏天。

sentences.en: When elections ushered in a bunch of self-described reformers.
sentences.zh: 选举迎来了一批自称改革派的人。

sentences.en: Ever since, the party has been in the grip of a bruising, chaotic, and sometimes thrilling fight.
sentences.zh: 从那以后，该党一直处于一场激烈、混乱，有时又令人兴奋的斗争中。

sentences.en: In the latest episode of Metro, with me, Sarah Koenig, stories of people trying to maintain their influence and losing control along the way.
sentences.zh: 在最新一期的《地铁》节目中，我和莎拉·凯尼格将讲述人们试图维持影响力却在过程中失去控制的故事。

sentences.en: Metro.
sentences.zh: 《地铁》。

sentences.en: Listen wherever you get your podcasts.
sentences.zh: 在任何你获取播客的地方收听。

sentences.en: We'll see you next time.
sentences.zh: 我们下次见。

sentences.en: We'll see you next time.
sentences.zh: 我们下次见。

sentences.en: Thank you.
sentences.zh: 谢谢。
